reference.source: Williams Obstetrics / RCOG and FIGO gestational trophoblastic disease guidance
clinicalPearls: GTN is the malignant end of the trophoblastic disease spectrum and includes invasive mole, choriocarcinoma, placental site trophoblastic tumour, and epithelioid trophoblastic tumour
It most often follows a hydatidiform mole but can arise after any pregnancy event
Diagnosis after molar pregnancy is usually made on beta-hCG criteria, such as a plateau or rise across defined measurements, rather than on histology
Beta-hCG is central to diagnosis, staging, monitoring treatment response, and detecting relapse for most subtypes
The FIGO anatomical stage and the modified WHO prognostic score together separate low-risk from high-risk disease and guide therapy
Low-risk disease is generally treated with single-agent methotrexate-based chemotherapy, while high-risk disease requires multi-agent regimens
Placental site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumours secrete relatively little hCG, are less chemosensitive, and are treated primarily with surgery
Care through a specialist trophoblastic centre with structured surveillance yields high cure rates
reference.pathophysiology: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia represents persistent or malignant proliferation of trophoblast following a molar or non-molar pregnancy. Invasive mole reflects molar villi penetrating the myometrium, whereas choriocarcinoma is frankly malignant trophoblast without villi that invades vasculature and metastasises early. Placental site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumours arise from intermediate trophoblast, grow more indolently, produce little beta-hCG, and are relatively chemoresistant. Most subtypes secrete beta-hCG in proportion to tumour burden, providing a sensitive marker, and the neoplastic tissue is often highly vascular with a tendency to haemorrhage and, for choriocarcinoma, to spread to lungs, brain, and liver.
additionalDifferentials: Persistent or retained products of conception
Pituitary or heterophile sources of a false-positive hCG
additionalInvestigations: Pelvic ultrasound with Doppler for uterine disease and vascularity
Cross-sectional imaging of brain, abdomen, and pelvis for staging when indicated
Full blood count, renal and liver function before chemotherapy
Histology where surgical specimens are available, particularly for placental site and epithelioid tumours
redFlags: Beta-hCG plateau or rise, or new symptoms, after evacuation of a mole
Haemoptysis, breathlessness, or neurological features suggesting metastatic choriocarcinoma
Heavy uterine or intraperitoneal haemorrhage from vascular tumour
High-risk prognostic score requiring urgent multi-agent chemotherapy
reference.prognosis: Most gestational trophoblastic neoplasia is curable, with low-risk disease approaching universal cure and high-risk disease achieving high survival through risk-adapted chemotherapy at specialist centres. Placental site and epithelioid tumours have a less favourable, more surgery-dependent course.
pitfalls: Not following beta-hCG after molar pregnancy and missing early progression
Applying hCG-based monitoring uncritically to placental site tumours, which secrete little hCG
Treating high-risk disease with single-agent chemotherapy and inducing resistance
Biopsying a highly vascular uterine tumour and provoking major haemorrhage
references: RCOG guidance on gestational trophoblastic disease
FIGO staging and prognostic scoring for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia
management: Risk-stratify with the FIGO anatomical stage and modified WHO prognostic score to guide treatment intensity
Treat low-risk disease with single-agent methotrexate-based chemotherapy with folinic acid rescue
Treat high-risk disease with multi-agent chemotherapy such as the EMA/CO regimen
Consider surgery, including hysterectomy, for chemoresistant placental site or epithelioid tumours and for control of haemorrhage
Monitor treatment response and detect relapse with serial quantitative beta-hCG
Stage with chest, brain, and abdominopelvic imaging to direct risk-adapted therapy
Manage at a specialist trophoblastic centre and advise reliable contraception throughout follow-up
